name: Water stress (not enough water)
generic_advice: Water early morning or evening to reduce evaporation loss.
Add mulch (dry leaves/straw) around the base to retain soil moisture.
Check the root zone at 10-15cm depth — if dry, irrigate now.
escalate_if: wilting continues after two consecutive watering cycles

name: Waterlogging / root suffocation (too much water)
generic_advice: Improve field drainage — open a channel away from the plant if water is standing.
Avoid further irrigation until the topsoil dries out.
Loosen compacted soil around the base once it is dry enough to walk on.
escalate_if: roots smell foul or are visibly rotting when the plant is gently uprooted

name: Nitrogen deficiency
generic_advice: Nitrogen moves from old to new leaves first, so older/lower leaves yellow first — this is the classic sign.
Apply a balanced, locally recommended fertilizer or well-rotted compost/manure.
Heavy recent rain can wash nitrogen out of sandy soils — consider a split fertilizer schedule.
escalate_if: yellowing continues after one fertilizer application at the recommended dose

name: Iron/micronutrient deficiency (interveinal chlorosis)
generic_advice: New leaves yellowing while veins stay green usually points to iron or another micronutrient, not nitrogen.
This is common in alkaline or waterlogged soils where iron becomes less available to roots.
A soil test (free at your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra) confirms which micronutrient is short before you spend on inputs.
escalate_if: symptom does not improve after correcting soil drainage/pH

name: Potassium deficiency
generic_advice: Scorched, browning leaf edges/tips on older leaves is a classic potassium sign.
Wood ash or a potash-based fertilizer, applied per local recommendation, is the usual correction.
Confirm with a soil test before repeat applications.
escalate_if: browning spreads to the whole leaf rather than staying at the margin

name: Heat stress
generic_advice: Provide temporary shade netting during the hottest part of the day if feasible.
Increase watering frequency (smaller amounts, more often) during heat waves.
Avoid fertilizing during a heat spell — it can worsen stress.
escalate_if: leaves show scorched/bleached patches, not just curling

name: Fungal leaf disease (blight/spot family)
generic_advice: Remove and destroy (do not compost) visibly infected leaves to slow spread.
Improve airflow — wider plant spacing and pruning dense growth reduces humidity around leaves.
Avoid overhead watering in the evening; water at the base in the morning instead.
escalate_if: more than a quarter of the plant's leaves are affected, or it is spreading across the field

name: Bacterial disease
generic_advice: Avoid working in the field while leaves are wet — this spreads bacteria between plants.
Remove severely affected plants/leaves and dispose away from the field, not on the compost heap.
Disinfect tools between plants if pruning affected material.
escalate_if: lesions are spreading rapidly across many plants — this needs expert confirmation before any treatment

name: Viral disease (often pest-transmitted)
generic_advice: Viral diseases cannot be cured — management focuses on controlling the insect that spreads it (often whitefly or aphids).
Remove and destroy severely affected plants to reduce the source of spread.
This needs an expert/KVK visit to confirm — many viral symptoms look similar to nutrient or pest issues.
escalate_if: always — viral disease should be confirmed by an expert, not chemically treated on a guess

name: Sap-sucking pest (aphid/whitefly/mite family)
generic_advice: Check the underside of leaves — most sap-sucking pests hide there.
A strong jet of water can dislodge many of them without any chemical.
Yellow sticky traps help monitor and reduce flying pests like whitefly and aphids.
escalate_if: infestation covers most of the plant or is spreading across the field within days

name: Chewing pest (caterpillar/beetle family)
generic_advice: Hand-pick visible caterpillars/beetles in the early morning when they are easiest to spot.
Check field margins and weeds nearby — they often shelter these pests between feeding.
Encourage natural predators (birds, ladybirds) by avoiding broad chemical spraying.
escalate_if: damage is severe and spreading across many plants within a few days
